title: Holdout Cohort Pairing Debrief - Dec 2025
body:
Purpose:
This note summarizes the holdout-cohort pairing experiment run to compare the baseline (redwood-1.1) vs candidate (redwood-1.2-alpha-quant) across stratified user cohorts and prompt templates. Goal was to detect regressions and surface per-cohort tradeoffs before any rollout.

Quick summary: 
- Candidate shows a net win_rate of 58% vs baseline on the primary instruction-following metric across aggregate cohorts, with strongest gains on task-oriented prompts and small regressions on lengthy creative completions.
- Safety/hallucination regressions were observed in the "finance-fact-check" cohort (hallucination-rate +1.8 percentage points).
- Latency P95 increased from 180ms to 240ms for long-context (3k tokens) flows on the dedicated quantized nodes; cost-per-1k tokens decreased ~22%.
- Recommendation: proceed to a constrained canary (5% traffic) with automated kill-switch triggers (safety > 1% absolute increase OR end-to-end error rate +0.5%). Delay full rollout until targeted tuning on finance cohort examples.

Experiment design (short):
- Data: 6 holdout cohorts stratified by task and prompt family: task-orient (TODO lists, code edits), creative (stories/lyrics), instruction-rich (multi-step instructions), finance-fact-check, customer-support, long-context summarization. Each cohort had 1k held-out examples reserved from the onboarding promptset.
- Pairing: randomized pairwise assignment per example: candidate vs baseline, single-shot per example, paired-bootstrap to compute win_rates and 95% Bayesian credible intervals.
- Metrics: instruction-following score (0-1, human + automated heuristics), safety/hallucination-rate (binary label if hallucinated factual claim), BLEU-like overlap for summarization (not primary), latency P50/P95, cost-per-1k-tokens.
- Pass criteria: no cohort-level safety regression > 0.5pp, aggregate instruction-following win_rate >= 55% with lower 95% CI > 50%.

Win/Loss table (aggregated by cohort):
cohort,n_examples,candidate_wins,baseline_wins,ties,win_rate,delta_instruction_score
task-oriented,1000,620,330,50,0.65,+0.12
creative,1000,490,470,40,0.51,+0.03
instruction-rich,1000,580,380,40,0.60,+0.09
finance-fact-check,1000,420,540,40,0.43,-0.08
customer-support,1000,560,400,40,0.58,+0.07
long-context-summarize,1000,510,440,50,0.53,+0.04

Notes on interpretation:
- Task-oriented cohort is the largest uplift driver; manual review shows better slot-filling and fewer instruction-misreads.
- Finance cohort regression correlates with a tokenization/quantization artifact on numeric sequences; we observed truncated numeric tokens in 12 flagged examples. Root cause hypotheses below.
- Creative cohort is near parity; candidate tends toward shorter completions which sometimes reduces human-preferred creativity but improves conciseness.

Per-cohort heatmap highlights (qualitative):
- Task-oriented: consistent improvements on action-item extraction and code edit prompts.
- Instruction-rich: better multi-step planning but occasional premature termination at step boundaries.
- Finance: hallucinations are concentrated on multi-field aggregation tasks (e.g., "sum quarterly revenue" examples).
- Long-context: p95 latency increased primarily due to KV cache path changes in quant runtime; throughput improved for small requests.

Safety and regression triage:
- Hallucination-rate by cohort (baseline -> candidate): task-oriented 2.3% -> 1.9%; creative 3.1% -> 3.0%; finance 1.5% -> 3.3% (regression); customer-support 0.9% -> 0.8%.
- For finance cohort, we sampled 100 failure examples; 62 showed numeric token cutoff mid-number, 18 showed erroneously inferred external facts. Tentative cause: substring token boundary shifts after quantized embedding projection.
- Immediate mitigation options: 1) conservative detokenize patch for numeric tokens, 2) cohort-specific fallback to baseline for finance-related prompt tags, 3) prompt-level guardrails (explicit "do not infer missing numbers").

Operational metrics:
- Latency P50/P95 (ms): baseline 95/180 -> candidate 90/240 (small requests slightly faster, long-context P95 regressed).
- Cost: estimated inference compute cost down 22% on candidate due to 4-bit quant kernel efficiency.
- Error rate: end-to-end HTTP 5xx unchanged at 0.12% -> 0.13% (within noise).

Statistical notes:
- Win rates computed with paired-bootstrap (10k resamples) and Bayesian credible intervals reported in the appendix (see linked Confluence). We prioritized paired analysis to control per-example difficulty.
- Ties defined as delta instruction score within +/- 0.02.

Decision and recommended rollout path:
1) Canaries: 5% traffic split for 72 hours across non-finance cohorts only (task-oriented + instruction-rich + customer-support + creative + long-context), with a rollback if safety regression > 0.5pp in any observed cohort or if end-to-end error rate increases >0.5pp.
2) Finance gating: do not serve finance-fact-check cohort from candidate. Create an explicit cohort-routing rule to keep finance traffic on baseline until follow-up fixes.
3) Engineering action items: fix numeric tokenization edge-case (priority P0), add a detokenize safeguard, and re-run a 1k-sample smoke test for finance examples before expanding canary.
4) Observability: add a per-cohort hallucination alert + a dashboard card for numeric truncation examples.

Follow-ups (owners):
- Root cause and patch for numeric truncation: Priya Shah (due 2025-12-22).
- Canary run orchestration and automated rollback rule: Ethan Zhao + SRE (due 2025-12-20).
- Prompt guardrail design for finance prompts: Maya Chen (due 2025-12-21).
- Re-run holdout with patched runtime and update memo: Hannah Morales (due 2025-12-29).

Unresolved questions / open tickets:
- Is the numeric truncation exclusively a quant kernel artifact or exacerbated by our tokenizer updates? (JIRA-ML-3432)
- How will model calibration shifts affect downstream scoring for customer billing and analytics pipelines? Need a short experiment.
- Should we adopt cohort-specific fallback rules in the routing layer long-term, or aim to eliminate cohort disparities via model tuning?

Appendix pointers (quick):
- Full per-example CSV and bootstrap samples: linked in Confluence (see linked_artifacts).
- Human annotation guidelines used for instruction-following scoring included in the Confluence doc.
- Raw timing traces and kernel logs (internal S3 bucket link in Confluence).

Bottom line: candidate brings clear aggregate quality and cost wins but exposes a specific finance-facing regression that needs a small engineering fix and a conservative canary plan. Recommend targeted canary + patch-before-increase in traffic.

Notes to reviewers: please add comments inline for any cohort you care about; explicitly call out if you object to the finance holdback or the 5% canary size.

(End of debrief)
